user_scenario:
You are Sergeant First Class Thaddeus Okafor-Lindqvist, forty, an Army logistics NCO stationed at Fort Bragg, calling Ridgeline on your lunch break. You are polite, clipped and a bit impatient, the way you talk to any orderly room, and you like answers in dates. Ridgeline has had your Sandhills card account on military protection since last October. The paperwork you got says your next status review is due on October 15, and you want to get ahead of it: you are calling to have Ridgeline send you the request for the proof it needs for that review and to tell you exactly when that proof is due. You say that at the start, in a sentence or two.

Give identity details only as they are asked for. To be found, you give your phone number, 9105554263. To verify, you give the last four of your Social Security number, 4729; if one more detail is needed you give your date of birth, February 17, 1986 (1986-02-17), or your ZIP code, 28314. Your email is thaddeus.okafor.lindqvist@outlook.com if anyone asks, though you remind them you asked Ridgeline not to email you. You do not carry any Ridgeline reference numbers and tell the agent to look them up. Only if the agent asks about other accounts or recent paperwork do you mention that a Cape Fear Wireless bill was sent over to Ridgeline last month and that you phoned on October 2 to ask for the same military protection on it, and that you mailed in your newest orders, number ORDERS 4426-B-2026, at the start of October. You do not know balances or dates beyond that and leave them to the records. You know nothing about Ridgeline's internal rules and never suggest what should happen first.

You are fine with Ridgeline sending you whatever requests and letters go with your military protection by mail; you only want to hear what was sent and when each thing is due. If the agent tells you the Cape Fear request still needs its documentation request and that it is being sent, you say good, send it, and note the due date. If the agent explains that your protection on the card account has to be extended first and that the extension is something you book yourself in the portal on the orders you already sent, you agree to extend it; when the agent hands it over you book it with exactly the hold reference and number of days the agent gives you, and read back what the portal confirms. If something the agent quotes contradicts what the agent said a moment earlier, you ask them to check the records, but you never offer a number of your own.

When the agent tells you the review proof request has gone out and gives you its due date, you repeat the date, say thanks, and hang up; you have nothing else to raise.
